To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
EBV-miR expression levels are significantly higher in the early phase of IM and then decrease with disease progression.
the expression of viral and human miRNA is dynamic during primary EBV infections and that the expression of miRNAs is related to EBV replication and host immune responses.
the dynamic expression profiles of both EBV-miR and hsa-microRNAs were identified in IM caused by EBV infection.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the role of viral and cellular small non-coding RNAs in EBV infection, which is of great importance for understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis of EBV infection and for the development of novel diagnostic markers and therapeutic approaches.

the dynamic expression of viral and human miRNAs in EBV infection, which might provide a novel approach to understanding the pathogenic mechanism and developing new diagnostic markers for EBV-related diseases.
the dynamic expression of viral and host miRNAs in primary EBV infection, which may be helpful for the diagnosis and treatment of EBV infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

EBV-miR expression was significantly higher at early stage, but with a slower rate than that of viral load, and cellular miRNas of B cells and CD8+ T cell exhibited different expression pattern with time.
the expression profile of EBV and cellular miRNPs in IM caused by EBV infection was dynamic and complex.
EBV miRNAs are up-regulated in IM, but with the progression of the disease, they are gradually down-regulated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the viral miRNAs were up-regulated in IM, which was consistent with the increase of viral DNA.
EBV-miRNA and cellular miRNA expression patterns are differentially regulated in IM caused by the primary EBV infection in children.
viral and cellular miRNA expression profiles were dynamic during IM.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of viral and human miRNAs is highly correlated during primary EBV infections.
EBV-miR-16–1, 18–1, and miR-BHRFI-2–3p, 3p, 1–2–5P, and BART4-5P may be the biomarkers for EBV infection and EBV-miRNA–host miRNA interactions may play a role in the pathogenesis of EBV-related IM.

the dynamic expression of miRNAs in EBV infection is complex, and the expression levels of miR-BHR1-1, miR-BHR-2, miR-BAR13-1, miRNA-155-5P, miRNA-18B-5P and 181A-5P of B cells and T cells may be the biomarkers for the diagnosis of EBV infection.
